memory_candidates: In Arisaka-Das-Strassburger's paper, page 10's Lemma 4.7 parts (i) and (ii) display literally the same conclusion formula in the recovered PDF -- both a direct page render and pdftotext independently show this, so it is an observed source characteristic (not a rendering artifact of one extraction method), and one Lean lemma can discharge both citations.

In this codebase's nested-sequent development, OutputCtx.fillRhs and OutputCtx.fillFull are genuinely different filling shapes at the fm level (fillRhs's n=0 case wraps with a fixed top antecedent; fillFull's n=0 case is the identity, and its singleton case merges via a raw comma rather than a boxed antecedent) -- any soundness fact whose premise uses one operation and whose conclusion uses the other needs a dedicated bridging lemma, not a corollary of either operation's own congruence lemma alone. This affected Lemma 4.6's diaR/impR/boxL and Lemma 4.9's orL/impL/cut cases, all deferred rather than silently forced through the wrong operation.

For two-hypothesis (branching-rule) congruence facts built via nested deductionTheorem discharges, OutputCtx.fillRhs's uniform recursion (only the n=0 base case is special) is substantially simpler to handle than OutputCtx.fillFull's three-case recursion (which needs an extra and-uncurry combinator at the singleton case) -- prefer routing branching soundness facts through fillRhs's shape when the rule's actual index permits it.
